verdict.rationale: Semgrep's own docs have a dedicated pre-commit page. It states that the pre-commit framework can run semgrep when you commit changes, preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into Git history, which covers every element of the story directly. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the pre-commit hook in use, documented hook configuration details (e.g. the .pre-commit-config.yaml entry and commit-blocking behavior on findings).

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the scanner as a pre-commit hook so secrets and issues never enter my git history

citations.quote: The pre-commit framework can run semgrep when you commit changes. This is helpful in preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into your Git history.
The pre-commit framework can run `semgrep` when you commit changes.
